title: WfGg Radar operational discovery and controlled runtime evolution
problem: Maintain reliable WfGg Radar server discovery while preserving already validated collection data, production safety controls, and the targeted federated discovery workflow.
goals: Continue discovering Last War server clusters through targeted sequential @federated:<serverId> scans.
Preserve validated Collector history and avoid repeating already acquired server scans.
Use ChaCha DEV Project Control, Scheduler, Run Controller and registered Radar Runtime Adapter for runtime intervention.
Keep production changes bounded, approval-gated, reversible and independently observable.
non_goals: Do not change Last War game state or invoke mutating game commands.
Do not replace authoritative NAS persistence with VPS-local project storage.
Do not expose raw player data, credentials or runtime secrets.

current_change.purpose: Add a read-only one-region Seed Scout that tries small non-overlapping batches of candidate server IDs, without creating Collector cycles or enriching profiles, and returns an observed seed for the existing targeted @federated workflow.

acceptance_criteria: V6.19.3 build and tests pass on a pinned Git revision.
Pilot binaries and staged Cloudflare surfaces are SHA256 pinned before any runtime deployment.
Seed Scout creates zero Collector cycles, performs zero Collector ingestion, and performs zero profile enrichment.
Seed Scout uses only one map region per candidate and exposes aggregate server counts only.
Numeric proximity is used only to order candidate probes and never to infer cluster membership.
Production-deploy permission requires explicit human approval recorded in ChaCha DEV Evidence Ledger.
Radar Sentinel protection is restored after the pilot window and the production-release approval is revoked.
architecture_invariants: GitHub stores code, branches, CI and release artifacts.
ChaCha DEV on ChaChaVPS is the runtime orchestrator.
ChaChaNas remains authoritative persistent storage for project data and backups.
VPS is runtime-oriented and not the authoritative durable project store.
Producer and verifier responsibilities remain separated.
